reasoning: The mmap sink is real: ClaudeSessionScanner.swift:91 and CodexSessionScanner.swift:128 do use Data(contentsOf:options:[.mappedIfSafe]). But the only source is a process running as the same user with write access to ~/.claude/projects or ~/.codex/sessions (ClaudeSessionScanner.swift:58-66). Those directories belong to the user and are not a boundary another principal can cross. A process that already has that access can kill the app outright with kill(2), edit config.toml, or read the credentials, so a SIGBUS race gives it nothing it lacks. For benign cases, the scanner's own comment and memo logic treat transcripts as append-only (ClaudeSessionScanner.swift:75-77). No normal writer (Claude Code CLI or Codex CLI) shrinks a file mid-scan, so nobody reaches the truncation path in the default deploy. The source is not attacker-controlled across any boundary, so point 1 of the proof standard fails. At most this is a robustness bug in how the app reads files, not an exploitable vulnerability.
